newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Krupp - dollar rate shows fx correction over.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Krupp - dollar rate shows fx correction over.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Han-Juergen Krupp said the current dollar-mark level showed that foreign exchange rate corrections were over, and described recent forex moves as "unspectacular".

In an interview with Wirtschaftswoche magazine published on Thursday, but held on Tuesday afternoon, Krupp also said that the Bundesbank's monetary policy could not be used to steer foreign exchange markets. Asked to comment on the dollar's level at just below 1.80 marks, Krupp said: "We had a significant need to correct against the dollar. Against this background there has been no spectacular activity in the past weeks. The current level shows that the correction has been completed."
Krupp declined direct comment on the likely outcome of the Bundesbank's next council meeting on July 24.
"But one must see rationally; the domestic economy does not at present give any reason to alter interest rates," he said.
Krupp also said that it was not the Bundesbank's strategy to use interest rates to affect foreign exchange market developments.
"It was always the declared policy of the Bundesbank, that monetary policy in an anchor currency country cannot be used to exercise exchange rate policy and to influence exchange rates," Krupp said.
"I assume that the Bundesbank stands by that policy," he said, also noting that central banks no longer have full control of the external value of currencies.
"Therefore a reorganisation of the European currency system and a punctual start of monetary union are necessary."

Asked whether the German central bank's current interest rate policy was too loose, as some economists have begun to suggest of late, Krupp said: "I cannot see that at all. We must get the investment economy moving and for that we need low interest rates at the long end."
Critics of the Bundesbank were approaching the issue only from the point of view of currency exchange rates, he said.
"We should be happy that this is the case (low interest rates) and ensure that the situation remains that way as long as we have high unemployment and a weak domestic economy."
Krupp also said that there was no inflation risk in Germany.
"Despite the depreciation (of the mark) we have no current inflation risks," he said.
He downplayed the recent surge on the German share market, saying this reflected increased liquidity from pension funds and institutional investors and had nothing to do with currency exchange rates.
